_comment: Keyed by WORK ID, which is only unique per author - so one entry can serve two authors' works, and `brutus` deliberately does: Hortensius' single fragment is a passage of Cicero's Brutus, so both point at cicero/brut. verify.js prints a NOTE for any shared key. Which Latin Library page(s) each practice work's Latin comes from. Paths are relative to https://thelatinlibrary.com/ and get '.shtml' appended. Used by fetch_sources.js (to build the local text cache) and by verify.js (to check every Latin field verbatim). Add an entry whenever a new work is created.
_proofread: Proofreading-only third source, NOT fetched and NOT a source for the app's Latin: Poesia Latina, http://www.poesialatina.it/index.htm - Cicero at _ns/ProsaLat/Cic/<work>.html (OrProCael.html, OrInPison.html, ...). Consult it only when a word here looks like a typo. It prints classical orthography (u for consonantal v: uidetur, uitia, diuersisque; inl-/inr- for ill-/irr-), which is a convention and not a typo, and it carries real variant readings. Only plain non-words qualify for a fragment's `emend` field. This key holds a string, so fetch_sources.js (which only collects arrays) ignores it.
_caesar: CAESAR AND HIRTIUS, added v1.11.0. All four works print BRACKETED chapter numbers [n], so spans are free and no marker `fix` is needed. The Gallic War pages ALSO carry bare-digit SUBSECTION numbers inside each chapter ([13] 1 In omni Gallia ... 2 Plerique ...); the app prints those as bolded **1.** and normalise() strips both shapes. Work ids are deliberately distinct between the two authors: Caesar has bg-i..bg-vii, Hirtius has bellum-gallicum-viii, because sources.json is keyed by WORK ID and is shared across authors - a collision would silently give one of them the wrong page list.
_lucretius: LUCRETIUS, added v1.14.0. VERSE: the pages print a line number every five verses at the END of the line (`fruatur               45`) and lacunae as `* * *` lines; strip.js verseText() removes both, and extract_verse.js selects passages by verse number. The Latin Library TRANSPOSES Book I vv. 50-61 to after v. 135 (keeping their numbers), so a range must be resolved through the printed numbers, never by position. Line numbers are cross-checked against Perseus (tools/fetch_sections_perseus_verse.js).
_comicMetres: v1.15.3. The metre of each Plautus and Terence excerpt comes from Timothy J. Moore, The Meters of Roman Comedy (https://hdwlabs.artsci.wustl.edu/romancomedy/), which publishes the whole database as one TSV at /tsv/current.tsv. tools/comic_metres.js reads it from tools/.cache/moore-meters.tsv; re-fetch that file if it is missing. It is metre data, not Latin text, so it is not part of the verify.js chain, and no excerpt text comes from it. tools/scan_drama.js is the independent check: it scans from the spelling alone and can refute a metre, never prove one.
_verseNumberingNote: v1.15.5. The sixteen plays of Plautus and Terence that this app quotes, fetched ONLY so that tools/number_excerpts.js can work out the verse number of every line: the Latin Library prints a number every fifth verse, which is enough to number the rest by counting forward and backward from it. The key is not a work id, so verify.js never looks at these pages, and no excerpt text comes from them - the Latin in the bank was already taken from the same source. Note the two page names that are not what you would guess: Casina is plautus/cas and Adelphoe is ter.adel.html. Terence is published as .html, which is why a page may now carry its own extension.
_metreExamplesNote: v1.15.0. Pages fetched ONLY for the scansion examples on the metre reference pages (js/metres.js), not for any practice excerpt. The key is not a work id, so verify.js never looks at it; fetch_sources.js walks every array in this file, so the cache stays rebuildable and the provenance is recorded. tools/check_metre_quotes.js proves each quoted verse is verbatim. THE RULE (the user, v1.15.0): a metre page only shows example authors WHO ARE IN THE BANK - so the examples come from Ennius, Lucilius, Lucretius and Catullus, and Virgil, Horace and Martial stay out until they are added as authors. Only `catullus` is needed here, for Carmen 1, which is not itself an excerpt; every other example verse is quoted from js/fragments.js.

_notLive._comment: Nothing is waiting here right now: the four letter collections that used to sit in this block went live in v1.8.0 and are listed above. Keep the block for the next sourced-but-unused page, and keep the notes below. NOTE: cicero/adbrutum is only a table of contents - the letters themselves are on adbrutum1 and adbrutum2. CORRECTION (v1.7.5): this file used to claim the Verrines actio prima is not on TLL. It is - the slug is cicero/ver1, not verres.1, and the Divinatio is cicero/caecilium. All seven parts are live and are now listed above; the authoritative index is cicero/ver.shtml. Beware: ver1 prints 18 CHAPTER numbers as [1]-[18], not the 56 sections modern editions use, so cite that one by chapter.
